summary: Justin Hartley Moore was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed his Ph.D. at Columbia University under A. V. Williams Jackson and David P. Jackson, later teaching French (1908) and Romanic languages (1916) at the City College of New York.

Justin McDaniel works in Buddhist and religious studies. He has served as an Associate Professor of Religious Studies at the University of California, Riverside, and held the Edmund J. and Louise W. Kahn Endowed Professorship at the University of Pennsylvania (attested 2011–2026).

Justin Ritzinger is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Harvard University under Robert M. Gimello and Michael Puett, and has held positions at Oberlin College (attested 2013) and the University of Miami (2013).
Justin Shimeld is a philosopher who completed his PhD at the University of Tasmania, where he studied under doctoral supervisors Jeff Malpas and Sonam Thakchoe.

Justin Václav Prášek was an Iranian and Central Asian studies and history/archaeology scholar. He earned his Ph.D. at Charles University and also studied at the universities of Munich and Berlin in 1885. He taught Édouard Huber.
Justus Günther Grassmann studied at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg from around 1797 to 1801 and held a post at Marienstiftsgymnasium from 1806 to 1852.

Justus Olshausen was a linguist, Indologist, and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar. Educated at Kiel, Berlin, and Paris, he taught as a professor of Oriental languages at Kiel University (1823) and served as chief librarian and professor at Königsberg (1853–1858).
Justyna Wiśniewska-Singh is an Indologist and linguist. She completed her M.A. and Ph.D. at the University of Warsaw between 2001 and 2015, later holding a post there in 2016.
Jvala Singh is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who completed a PhD at the University of British Columbia (2018–2024). He was a lecturer at the University of California, Berkeley in 2021.
Jyotirindranath Tagore was active in linguistics and other fields. He received his education at the Hindu School and at Presidency University around 1864 to 1867.

János Harmatta was a scholar of Iranian, Central Asian, and Indo-European linguistics and Indology. Educated at Eötvös Loránd University (Ph.D. 1940), he became a professor there in 1952 and served as director at the Hungarian Academy of Sciences in 1968.

János Szerb was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his Ph.D. at Eötvös Loránd University, worked as a research associate and lecturer at the University of Vienna (1982), and conducted research at the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia (1984–1988).

Jérôme Ducor is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at Lausanne and Geneva (D. Litt.) under Jacques May, later working as a privat docent at Lausanne, senior lecturer at Geneva, and curator at the Musée d'ethnographie de Genève (1995–2019).

Józef Lączak was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Helena Willman-Grabowska at Jagiellonian University (M.A. 1952). He lectured at Eötvös Loránd University, the University of Warsaw, and Helsinki, later heading Jagiellonian University's Indian Department (1980–1989).

Józef Reczek was a linguist and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar. He studied at Jagiellonian University under Jerzy Kuryłowicz, Tadeusz Pobożniak, and Tadeusz Milewski, becoming a docent there in 1972.

Józef Szczepan Kowalewski was an Iranian, Central Asian, and Buddhist studies scholar and linguist. Educated at Vilnius and Kazan universities, he served as a professor and rector at Kazan Imperial University (1833–1860) and later as a professor and dean at the University of Warsaw.
Józef Turczyński held posts at the Ukrainian National Academy of Music (around 1915–1919) and the Chopin University of Music (around 1920–1939). He taught Constantin Régamey.

József Budenz was a linguist who studied under Theodor Benfey at the University of Göttingen. He served as a librarian at the Hungarian Academy of Sciences (1861) and full professor of Altaic comparative linguistics at Eötvös Loránd University (1868–1892).
József Schmidt was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at Eötvös Loránd University under Aurel Mayr, whom he succeeded, and served as a docent there from 1908 to 1920.

Jörg B. Quenzer works in Japanology and Buddhist studies. He has been affiliated with the University of Hamburg (attested 2016 and 2026) and served on the editorial board of Studies in Manuscript Cultures (attested 2016).
